Bail Bond Information for Stanislaus County

After booking into Stanislaus County jail, a judge typically sets bail at arraignment (often within 24–72 hours). Families often work with a licensed bail bondsman. A common commercial bond fee is about 10% of the bail amount (non-refundable). Example: $10,000 bail → roughly $1,000 premium, subject to local rules.

If the person cannot afford bail, they may request a reduction hearing or public defender.

For hearing schedules, contact the Stanislaus County court.

Visitation Rules at Stanislaus County Jail

Policies vary. Before visiting Stanislaus County Public Safety Center, confirm:

  • Approved ID: Government-issued photo ID
  • Hours: Call Stanislaus County Sheriff's Department for the current schedule
  • Dress code: Facilities restrict clothing that resembles uniforms
  • Video visits: Many jails offer remote options — ask when you call
  • Children: Minors usually need an accompanying adult

What to Expect After Arrest in Stanislaus County

Typical steps after arrest in Stanislaus County:

  1. Booking — fingerprints, photo, property inventory
  2. Medical screening — before general population housing
  3. Classification — housing based on charges and history
  4. Arraignment — first court appearance; bail often set here
  5. Transfer — serious cases may move to a state facility

Frequently Asked Questions — Stanislaus County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Stanislaus County jail?

Start with the official Stanislaus County inmate roster. You can also call Stanislaus County Sheriff's Department at (209) 525-5630. Online records often lag booking by a few hours.

What is the phone number for Stanislaus County Public Safety Center?

Contact Stanislaus County Sheriff's Department at (209) 525-5630. Facility address on file: 200 E Hackett Rd, Modesto, CA 95358.

How long does booking take in Stanislaus County?

Booking commonly takes 2–8 hours depending on volume at Stanislaus County Public Safety Center. Weekends and holidays can delay when a name appears in any published system. If urgent, call the facility directly rather than waiting on a website refresh.

Can I visit an inmate at Stanislaus County jail?

Usually yes if the person is eligible and the facility is accepting visits. The main facility listed is Stanislaus County Public Safety Center at 200 E Hackett Rd, Modesto, CA 95358. Bring government photo ID and confirm hours and dress code with Stanislaus County Sheriff's Department before you go. Video visitation may be offered.

What if the person is not listed in the county system?

They may have been released, transferred, or booked under a different name spelling. Check California Department of Corrections and the Federal BOP locator for federal custody. Then call Stanislaus County Sheriff's Department to confirm.

How do I send money to someone at Stanislaus County Public Safety Center?

Ask Stanislaus County Public Safety Center which commissary vendor they use (often JPay, Securus, or Access Corrections) when you call (209) 525-5630. Limits and fees vary by facility — confirm before sending money.
